rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1<U+2013>2.4 <U+2013> three-season (2018<U+2013>2020) field experiment in a 2.1 ha young almond orchard in Hell<U+00ED>n (Spain) with five treatments in three randomized blocks, Sentinel-2 imagery and ground measurements. Q2: Abstract, Sections 3.1.1, 3.2, Conclusion <U+2013> severe sustained deficit irrigation (33% ETc) produced lower NDVI/SAVI, more negative <U+03A8>stem and smaller tree dimensions than full irrigation (about 13%, 23% and 14% lower respectively), while moderate deficit (67% ETc) did not differ from control; authors conclude that combining remote-sensing indexes with physiological measurements is suitable for assessing almond response to irrigation management. Q3: Sections 2.2 and 2.4 <U+2013> effect of severe deficit shown independently by satellite vegetation indexes (Sentinel-2 NDVI/SAVI) and by ground pressure-chamber <U+03A8>stem plus manual trunk perimeter and canopy diameter measurements, all showing the same treatment ranking (Figs 6, 9). Q4: Sections 3.2<U+2013>3.3 and Discussion <U+2013> the study measures the intermediate variables (plant water status, trunk perimeter, canopy cover) and shows that VI changes track structural canopy differences (logarithmic VI<U+2013>trunk perimeter and VI<U+2013>canopy cover relationships, R2 0.80<U+2013>0.95, Fig. 10), i.e. stress is captured by VIs through reduced canopy expansion. Q8: Discussion <U+2013> VIs showed low correlation with <U+03A8>stem, highlighting the limitation of NDVI/SAVI for detecting short-term water-status variations; 10 m Sentinel-2 resolution cannot separate tree canopy, bare soil and cover crop in heterogeneous pixels; discrepancies with other studies attributed to the short duration and young trees of this experiment. Q9: Figs 6<U+2013>9 captions <U+2013> error bars represent the standard error of treatment means for NDVI, SAVI, <U+03A8>stem, trunk perimeter and canopy diameter.
rows.notes: The study supports the diagnostic part of the passage (severe deficit detected via VIs and <U+03A8>stem, with the exact 13%/23%/14% reductions). However, the passage's extension to 'defining operational thresholds to adjust irrigation scheduling and prevent yield losses' is not supported: the study reports no yield data, derives no irrigation thresholds and does not test any scheduling adjustment; the crop_production function is therefore only indirectly addressed. Q7 'no': the study notes that VI<U+2013>morphology relationships depend on soil management (separate VC and BS relationships recommended) and that only severe, not moderate, deficit was detectable, but these are reported as findings/variations rather than stated requirements for the diagnostic effect. Single site, single crop, plot scale (2.1 ha orchard).

notes: Full text available; supplementary tables (S1<U+2013>S6) referenced but not included. Study is a three-year single-orchard field trial in semi-arid Spain; it contains no yield measurements, so any claim about preventing yield losses or deriving irrigation thresholds goes beyond its own results.
